tickets.desc: Ben Kindel o1.5 SOG -115, $3.50, pays $6.54 (PIT @ VGK 10:00 PM ET)
tickets.why: Kindel has 2+ shots in all 7 games this season (2,2,2,3,2,2,5 newest first; LineMate L9 8/9, away 4/5), averaging 2.57 SOG, so the 1.5 line sits about a full shot under his average. He is a full-role center at 15 to 19.5 minutes with a power-play goal and LineMate has him 8/9 without injured D Ryan Graves. VGK is a heavy -200 home favorite, so PIT should be chasing and shooting; PIT averages 28.8 shots per game. He is not on any injury report. Risks: PIT is on a back-to-back (lost 5-2 at COL Friday, Kindel 14:57 TOI) and his late-2025-26 call-up games were mostly 1 shot, so this leans on the current-season role, not a long history. Hard Rock price via LineMate.

legs.why: Kyrou has been at 2 or fewer shots in 6 of 7 games this season (3,1,1,0,1,1,2 newest first, 1.3 per game) and in 13 of his last 15 across both seasons (LineMate L14 13/14, home 10/11). He is playing only 11 to 15 minutes a night, and NJ allows just 25.0 shots per game, fourth-fewest. Not on the injury report. Risk: Pierre-Luc Dubois is out sick, which could bump Kyrou up the lineup; he had 3 shots in 15:15 last game, so the cushion is about one shot.

STL is actually the moneyline favorite (-115), so +1.5 only loses if the Blues lose by 2 or more. LineMate has STL +1.5 covering 18 of 20 away and 4 of 4 last 4. NSH has won only one game by 2+ all season (5-2 at MTL), and 4 of Nashville's 7 games were decided by one goal (three in OT or a shootout). NSH is projected to start Justus Annunen, who hasn't played an NHL game this season. STL's Buchnevich is day-to-day (personal), the only notable absence. Risk: an empty-net goal turning a one-goal loss into two.

runners_up.why: The Rays lose this only if Cleveland leads by 2+ after five innings. Nick Martinez threw 13 scoreless innings in two starts against CLE this year, and Cleveland is running a bullpen game (Shawn Armstrong opens). First-five totals in this series have been 2, 3 and 5. LineMate shows TB +1.5 F5 covering 6 of 6 vs CLE. Savant batter-vs-pitcher vs Martinez is all tiny samples with no home runs: Kwan 3-for-7 (xBA .198), Ramírez 1-for-11 (xBA .116), DeLauter 1-for-3, Adell 0-for-3 with a walk, Lowe 2-for-6. Weather is fine: about 45°F at first pitch, wind 3 to 4 mph from the southwest, 0% rain, and the cold favors pitching. Lineups aren't confirmed yet. Risk: Martinez has an early hook (3.2 and 2.2 innings in his last two starts), so TB's fully rested bullpen has to cover innings 4 and 5.

VAN is 2-6-1 with 7 losses in its last 8, gives up 4.56 goals and 32.4 shots per game, and generates only 21.9 shots (second-fewest). TB has won 4 of 4 at home and 5 of its last 6 (LineMate). Demko is on IR, so VAN starts Meriläinen (projected). The moneyline counts overtime, so a tie through regulation can still cash.

Roslovic has 2+ shots in all 8 games this season (5,2,5,3,4,2,2,2 newest first; LineMate home 7/7) and in 12 of his last 15 across both seasons, averaging 3.1 shots on 15 to 19 minutes. John Tavares is day-to-day after getting hurt Thursday, which could add center minutes. NYI allows 26.0 shots per game.

Dobson was at 2 or fewer shots in 6 of 7 games this season and 12 of his last 15 (LineMate L17 14/17, vs BUF 6/6, home 9/11). BUF allows only 24.6 shots per game. Risk: he had 5 shots in his most recent game, and Matheson is day-to-day, which could mean more minutes.

Gritsyuk has 2+ shots in 6 of 7 games this season (2,2,2,1,2,2,2) and 12 of his last 15 (LineMate L14 12/14, away 6/7, 9/10 without Connor Brown). His ice time is climbing (16:56 and 19:27 in his last two). NJ leads the NHL at 35.6 shots per game, and WSH allows 29.4. Brown is out, so his role holds. The cushion is thin since he has a lot of exact 2s.
